extracted.intended_audience: authors seeking literary representation (writers querying a literary agent)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and wish-list from a literary agent (Stephen Barr) describing the kinds of manuscripts he wants and how to submit queries; includes genre preferences, tonal/voice desiderata, and submission mechanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adult fiction that rewards the reader line-by-line
rubrics_metrics.description: adult fiction that rewards the reader line-by-line and handcuffs humor and tragedy to the same radiator, like Maggie Thrash’s Rainbow Black (other recent favorites include The Searcher, Five Decembers, Lonesome Dove, and The Night Watchman)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given to illustrate the tonal and craft level desired: strong sentence-level writing, an ability to blend humor and tragedy. Recent favorites provided as reference points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bonkers high-concept novels with a speculative tilt
rubrics_metrics.description: bonkers high-concept novels with a speculative tilt (time loops and the like!)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeks high-concept premises that also have speculative elements — playful/ambitious conceptual hooks such as time loops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audacious, experimental mysteries, fantasies and psychological suspense
rubrics_metrics.description: audacious, experimental mysteries, fantasies and psychological suspense
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefers work that pushes formal/genre boundaries and experiments with structure, voice, or conceit within mystery/fantasy/suspense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intricate, heart-on-its-sleeve, voice-abundant YA
rubrics_metrics.description: intricate, heart-on-its-sleeve, voice-abundant YA like King Dork or Baby & Solo (bonus points for unrequited love stories!)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wants YA with a strong distinctive voice and emotional openness; explicitly rewards unrequited-love storylines as a bonus element. Examples cited as tonal models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fantastical or contemporary middle grade tackling heavy themes optimistically
rubrics_metrics.description: fantastical or contemporary middle grade that takes on heavy themes with an optimistic, eccentric touch (like Eli Brown’s Oddity)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Middle grade should handle serious subjects but retain optimism and eccentricity; reference title provided as example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picture books that are sweet, silly, and/or heartbreaking from adventurous author/illustrators
rubrics_metrics.description: sweet and/or silly and/or heartbreaking picture books from adventurous author/illustrators
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeks picture books across a range of emotional registers but from creators willing to take risks or be adventurous in voice/illustration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unexpected memoirs with itchy voices
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Looking for memoir with a fresh, restless, attention-grabbing voice — something surprising rather than conventional memoir tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative non-fiction that tackles hard-to-tackle issues
rubrics_metrics.description: narrative non-fiction that tackles hard-to-tackle issues, like Monsters: A Fan’s Dilemma
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefers narrative nonfiction that engages difficult or fraught topics with rigor and narrative skill; example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detective stories that bend reality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open to mystery/detective fiction that mixes genre conventions with reality-bending or speculative elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ghost stories that blow reality to hell
rubrics_metrics.description: ghost stories that blow reality to hell
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wants ghost stories that are bold, destabilizing, and willing to radically subvert 'realistic' expectations — high tolerance for weirdness and intensity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secret Book X / curveballs
rubrics_metrics.description: Secret Book X (I don’t know what Secret Book X is, but suffice it to say, I’m open to the occasional curveball).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent expressly welcomes occasional unusual or unexpected projects outside listed categories — be bold with curveball submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method: email a query to sbarr@writershouse.com
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should be emailed to sbarr@writershouse.com. You can send me a query letter by e-mail, and just make sure to include the first five or ten pages of your manuscript, then fire away!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required submission mechanics: email the query letter and attach/include the first 5–10 pages of the manuscript. This is the explicit submission instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response-time expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: I promise to fire back, hopefully within two weeks’ time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can expect a response within approximately two weeks (not a guarantee, but the stated target).

rubrics_metrics.name: Areas/age-levels represented
rubrics_metrics.description: I’ve been with Writers House ... and I’m a pretty omnivorous agent, with both an adult list (mostly literary and commercial fiction, as well as journalistic non-fiction) and a children’s list (everything from picture books to young adult).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the agent represents both adult and children’s markets; useful for authors to self-select whether their work fits his lists (adult literary/commercial, journalistic nonfiction; picture books through YA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific fiction and non-fiction categories accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiction: Children's, Graphic Novel, LGBTQ, Literary, Middle Grade, Picture Books, Science Fiction, Young Adult. Non-Fiction: Journalism, Memoir, Pop Culture, Psychology, Science, Sports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit list of genres/categories the agent handles — authors should ensure their work falls into one of these categories when querying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favorite sub-genres / preference list
rubrics_metrics.description: Favorite sub-genres: Adult, Commercial and Literary, Contemporary YA, Domestic Suspense/Thriller, Fantasy Grounded in Reality, High-Concept Literary Commercial Fiction, Narrative Nonfiction, Psychological Thrillers, book club fiction, children's graphic novels, crossover adult, epistolary novels, literary suspense
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long list of preferred sub-genres that further refines the agent’s taste; authors can use these as signals of likely fit and examples to frame their query pitch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemplar/aspirational titles the agent would like 'the next' of
rubrics_metrics.description: I’d like the next… The Searcher, Jon Ronson, Christoph Neimann, The Blind Assassin, The World According to Garp, City Dog, Country Frog, Dear Mr. Henshaw
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides concrete title references to convey tone, scope, or audience he’s seeking. Use these as comparative hooks in a query if genuinely appropriate.
